title: Crawler throughput collapses on big sites
description: Your crawler shards its frontier by hash(full URL) across 40 nodes, each running a FIFO queue. To be polite, each node checks a shared Redis key 'last fetch time per host' and re-queues URLs whose host was fetched in the last second. Throughput is a third of target, Redis is saturated, and some large sites still report bursts of 20 requests per second. What is the best change?

options.text: Increase the Redis cluster size and shorten the per-host delay to 200 ms
options.explanation: More Redis capacity treats the symptom; the shared check-then-fetch is still racy across nodes (hence the bursts), and cutting the delay makes the crawler less polite.

options.text: Replace the FIFO with a Kafka topic partitioned by URL hash so ordering is durable
options.explanation: Durability is not the problem. Partitioning by URL hash still spreads one host across many consumers, and Kafka cannot reorder messages by host eligibility time.

options.text: Shard the frontier by host, keep per-host back queues on each shard, and pick ready hosts from a min-heap of next-eligible times
options.explanation: All URLs for a host live on one shard, so politeness is enforced locally without a shared store, and the heap means workers only take hosts that are ready, ending the re-queue churn.

options.text: Add more fetcher nodes so the re-queued URLs are retried sooner
options.explanation: More fetchers increase churn and contention on the shared check; the bottleneck is scheduling, not fetch capacity.
